issues.issue: The grant is simultaneously "unconditional and irrevocable" and "subject only to the terms of this Policy", so the reach of the guarantee turns on whether 'unconditionally' adds anything beyond the Policy's conditions. A court could be asked whether the promise of 'full and complete payment' is qualified or absolute.

The grant promises 'full and complete payment of the Scheduled Payments', while the Endorsement's 'Scheduled Payment' definition (c029) and the exclusions paragraph (c008) strip out large categories of amounts and limit payment to the Deficiency Amount. Whether the grant or the definitional carve-outs governs is a whole-instrument question.

The body sets payment on the later of one Business Day after receipt or the Business Day Scheduled Payments are due, while the Endorsement (c035) sets 12:00 noon on the first Business Day after receipt or the Payment Date to which the Deficiency Amount relates; the precedence clause (c058) resolves but presupposes the mismatch.

Subrogation 'to the extent of any payment' sits against the Endorsement's subordination clause (c044), which makes any subrogation rights junior to full payment of the Owners. The interaction of the two is a plausible construction question.

The body conditions Avoided Payment coverage on a 'final order' and on funds 'not otherwise available', whereas the Endorsement definition (c015) requires a 'final, nonappealable order' and c037 requires the appeal period to have expired, with no 'other funds' proviso. The two statements of the same coverage do not line up.

The Policy 'shall not be cancelled or revoked by XLCA for any reason'; whether 'cancelled or revoked' also forecloses rescission or avoidance at law (e.g., for fraud in the inducement) is genuinely open on the words. The scope of 'for any reason' against the specific example of unpaid premium is the point of dispute.

'The premium on this Policy is nonrefundable for any reason' is a short absolute phrase whose reach — whether it survives rescission or avoidance of the Policy itself — cannot be determined from the words. 'For any reason' is the term in issue.

The exclusion pairs specific carve-outs (prepayment, acceleration, tax shortfalls) with the general bar on 'any risk other than Nonpayment and Avoided Payment', and the 'including' tail leaves the catch-all's reach uncertain. Whether the enumerated items limit or merely illustrate the general exclusion is a classic ejusdem generis question.

This sends undefined terms to the Endorsement, while the Endorsement (c014) sends them on to the Indenture and the precedence clause (c058) makes the Endorsement paramount; the chain is workable but layered. A meaning-hunting dispute would have to reconcile all three.

The Endorsement identifies the Insured Obligations as $507,837,000 Class A-1 and $132,870,000 Class A-2 Notes, while the face of the Policy recites a different Class A figure. Any discrepancy between the two descriptions of the same insured securities would have to be reconciled.

This defines 'Avoided Payment' as a payment actually returned by a holder under a final, nonappealable order, but the operative Avoided Payment paragraph (c037) separately defines the same quoted term as a payment an Owner 'is required to return' following a Preference Event. Two competing definitions of one defined term in the same instrument.

The definition turns on days when 'the jurisdiction in which' several named parties are located is authorized to close, but those parties may sit in different jurisdictions and the clause does not say whether one or all controls. 'The jurisdiction in which ... is located' is the ambiguous phrase.

The definition twice ends an enumeration with 'or similar proceedings', leaving the catch-all's reach against the listed bankruptcy/insolvency/reorganization specifics uncertain. Whether a given foreign or regulatory proceeding is 'similar' is exactly the ejusdem generis question.

The definition names 'EMC Mortgage Company, as sponsor' and 'the Depositor' without further identification, so the identity of the sponsor party (and of the Depositor) rests on a name that may not match the actual entity. A misnaming of a party to the incorporated Insurance Agreement is a construable mechanical defect.

The definition gives two measures at once — the portion of Scheduled Payments unpaid by reason of Nonpayment, and an amount 'equal to the related Deficiency Amount' — which need not coincide because the Deficiency Amount includes Insured Note Charge-off Amounts. Which limb controls is left open.

The definition rests entirely on 'Charge-Off Amounts' allocated to the Note Principal Balance, a term supplied only by the Indenture through c014, so its content is not fixed within the instrument. Its interaction with the Deficiency Amount definition (c017) would have to be worked out.

The definition speaks of amounts paid by 'the Note Insurer', a term the Policy never defines, while the operative paragraphs consistently call the insurer 'XLCA'. Equating the two requires resort to the Indenture via c014.

The list of entity types is joined by 'and' rather than 'or' ('a trust, an unincorporated organizations, and a government'), which on its face makes the definition conjunctive; the plural 'organizations' compounds the slip. The conjunction is a mechanical error affecting who counts as a Person.

The definition imports the interest rate and 'amounts then due and owing' from the Insurance Agreement, and the preserved right to Reimbursement Amounts (c045) sits against the subordination clause (c044). The priority of reimbursement against Owner payments is left to be worked out across provisions.

After excluding accelerated payments due to 'any optional redemption, in whole or in part, or any other cause', the catch-all's reach against the specific redemption example is uncertain, and the following five-item exclusion list ('any other sum payable ... by reason of any default') compounds it. The general-versus-specific tension is on the face of the definition.

The Term ends on the 'first date' on which three cumulative conditions are met, yet the closing proviso ('provided, further') fixes a different termination date keyed to the insurer's payments, and there is no earlier proviso for it to follow. Which of the two termination triggers governs is left open.

'As soon as reasonably practicable' for delivery of the original notice sets no benchmark and no consequence for delay. Whether late delivery of the original defeats a faxed claim cannot be answered from the words.

The deemed-receipt rule fixes constructive receipt at 9:00 a.m. the next Business Day, while the notices clause (c049) says every Payment Notice 'shall be effective only upon actual receipt by XLCA'. The two receipt rules cannot both be applied literally to the same notice.

This sets payment at 12:00 noon on the first Business Day after receipt or on the Payment Date to which the Deficiency Amount relates, whereas the Policy body (c002) states the obligation as one Business Day after receipt or the Business Day Scheduled Payments are due. The two timing rules are stated differently for the same obligation.

The delivery conditions are labelled (x), (y) and (z) but the middle label is missing from the text, and later paragraphs (c038, c040) cross-refer to 'clauses (x) through (z)'. The mislabelling leaves the identity of the required documents to be reconstructed.

This paragraph defines 'Avoided Payment' as a payment an Owner is required to return following a Preference Event, while the Endorsement definition (c015) requires a payment actually returned under a final, nonappealable order. The same defined term carries two different triggers.

The deemed-receipt rule for Avoided Payment documents conflicts with the notices clause (c049), which makes every presentation and delivery 'effective only upon actual receipt by XLCA'. Constructive and actual receipt cannot both control the same delivery.

The proviso cross-refers to 'the items referred to in clauses (x), (y) and (z) of the preceding paragraph', but the preceding paragraph (c037) does not carry a (y) label. The cross-reference does not match the text it points to.
